entry.title: Why x402 Doesn't Support USDT (But USDT0 Changes Everything)
entry.summary:
This article was originally published on PayIn Blog. Visit for more articles about x402 and stablecoin payments.
If you've explored the x402 protocol, you've noticed it exclusively supports USDC—not USDT. The reason is entirely technical: USDT doesn't implement the smart contract functions that x402 requires. x402 payments on EVM chains rely on ERC-3009, which enables gasless, signature-based transfers. USDT's contract only implements standard ERC-20 functions—no transferWithAuthorization, no permit.
Feature USDT USDC
Standard ERC-20 ✅ ✅
ERC-3009 ❌ ✅
ERC-2612 (permit) ❌ ✅
Gasless transfers ❌ ✅
x402 compatible ❌ ✅
With USDC: User clicks "Pay" → Signs in wallet → Instant response → Done With USDT: User clicks "Pay" → Approves → Waits → Clicks again → Transfers → Waits → Done In January 2025, Tether launched USDT0—an omnichain version built on LayerZero's OFT standard. The key difference? USDT0 implements ERC-3009 and ERC-2612.
Feature USDT (Original) USDT0
ERC-3009 ❌ ✅
ERC-2612 ❌ ✅
Gasless transfers ❌ ✅
x402 compatible ❌ ✅ (potentially)
Cross-chain native ❌ ✅
USDT0 has processed over $50 billion across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Sei, HyperLiquid, Solana, and more. Dual DVN Validation $6M Bug Bounty OpenZeppelin Audited Traditional USDT remains incompatible with x402, but USDT0 opens the door to Tether-based x402 payments. For builders: start with USDC for proven compatibility. ERC-3009: The Protocol Behind x402 Payments x402 Facilitators Solana's Authorization Mechanism x402 Developer's Guide The x402 protocol's USDC focus isn't about preference—it's about capability. With USDT0's ERC-3009 support, the future of HTTP-native payments is multi-stablecoin.
